questions.q: What is the real pattern this lesson describes for automated incident creation?
options: A PowerShell script authenticates and POSTs a structured payload to a ticketing system's REST API, receiving a ticket reference back
SQL Server Agent automatically opens tickets with no scripting involved
A DBA must always manually type the incident into the ticketing system
Incident creation can only happen through email, never an API
questions.explain: The pattern mirrors the earlier webhook pattern: authenticate, POST a payload, get a reference back — just aimed at a ticketing API instead of a chat webhook.

questions.q: Which two ticketing/incident-management products does the lesson name as real, widely used examples?
options: ServiceNow and Jira
Power BI and Grafana
Terraform and Bicep
Teams and Slack
questions.explain: ServiceNow and Jira are named as real examples, while the lesson deliberately avoids locking to one product's exact current API.

questions.q: Why does the lesson avoid giving one universal code sample guaranteed to work for every ticketing system?
options: Exact field names and authentication approaches genuinely differ by product and by how an organization's instance is configured
Ticketing system APIs are all identical, so any sample would work everywhere
PowerShell cannot call any ticketing system's API
REST APIs are incompatible with PowerShell's Invoke-RestMethod cmdlet
questions.explain: The lesson is honest that this genuinely requires consulting your own organization's specific API documentation.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what makes an automated incident description actually useful to a responder?
options: Naming the specific instance and check, the metric value against its threshold, and a timestamp
Only the word 'error' with no further detail
The name of the PowerShell script file that generated it
A random ticket number with no description at all
questions.explain: The lesson's better example puts the instance, the specific metric value, and the threshold right in the incident title.

questions.q: Structurally, how does calling a ticketing system's REST API compare to the Teams/Slack webhook pattern from the previous lesson?
options: It's the same basic shape — build a payload, POST it with Invoke-RestMethod, get a response back
It requires an entirely different scripting language
Ticketing APIs cannot be called from PowerShell at all
Webhooks and ticketing APIs share no similarities whatsoever
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly draws the parallel to the webhook pattern covered in the previous lesson.
